description: Mechanical cross-check of contraction_separator_integration.md Parts VI-VII: CB3's three exact cases (clean 2-attachment; the S5 cut-vertex coincidence, cited not re-derived; the genuinely new >=3-attachment degree-loss case), and the paired topological-K4 union arithmetic (2*ell+1 always safe; 2*ell+2 unsafe exactly at ell=2^j-1).
scope_note: Does not re-derive S5, T1, or T2 (all cited by name from lemmas.md/two_cut.md). Checks the structural mechanics CB3' actually reduces to: 2-connectivity and internal-degree preservation in the clean case, and the exact internal-degree LOSS phenomenon in the >=3-attachment case that motivates naming it a genuinely new failure mode rather than misapplying Type A/B/C. Kept separate from the seven prior contraction verifiers, none of which are touched.
note_on_python_version: Same environment note as prior manifests: requirements.txt/.python-version pin CPython 3.14.6, unavailable in this container; this run used 3.13.12 with networkx==3.6.1 (matches requirements.txt's pin exactly).
detector_agreement: The CB3 case checks use networkx.is_biconnected for the 2-connectivity claim (independent of this project's own cycle-detection code, a genuinely separate library routine) and direct adjacency-dict degree counting for the internal-degree claims. The paired-K4 arithmetic is checked by direct power-of-two testing against the symbolic prediction (ell=2^j-1 exactly). 0 disagreements.
completed_range: All three CB3 case gadgets and the full ell in {2,...,19} range processed to completion; this is a small, deterministic set of explicit illustrative constructions plus a bounded arithmetic sweep, not a search or census -- consistent with contraction_separator_integration.md Part X's explicit decision not to launch broad computation this pass.
